links.reason: Acts repeats the call “go to the land I will show you”; in Genesis, the LORD says it to Abram.
Acts repeats “all the families of the earth will be blessed”; Genesis has these words after “I will bless those who bless you.”
Acts says God promised the land to Abraham’s descendants; Genesis says “all the land that you see” goes “to you and your offspring forever.”
Acts repeats that the descendants will be “enslaved and mistreated four hundred years”; Genesis records the LORD saying this to Abram.
Acts says God will “punish the nation that enslaves them”; Genesis says the LORD will judge the nation, and afterward they will depart.
Acts says God promised the land to Abraham and his descendants; Genesis says “all the land of Canaan” will be “an eternal possession.”
Acts repeats the promise “Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed”; Genesis says “all nations of the earth.”
Acts repeats “Through your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed”; Genesis says “all nations of the earth will be blessed.”
Acts repeats “all the families of the earth will be blessed”; Genesis says it will be “through you and your offspring.”
Acts says Jacob and his relatives were “seventy-five in all”; Genesis counts Jacob’s family in Egypt as “seventy in all.”
Acts says Jacob and his relatives were “seventy-five in all”; Exodus says Jacob’s descendants “numbered seventy in all.”
Acts says a king “who knew nothing of Joseph” rose over Egypt; Exodus says a new king “who did not know Joseph” came to power.
Acts says a man abusing his neighbor pushed Moses aside; Exodus says Moses saw two Hebrews fighting and asked, “Why are you attacking your companion?”
Acts repeats “kill me as you killed the Egyptian”; Exodus has the man say it to Moses, who was then afraid.
Acts says Moses “fled to the land of Midian”; Exodus says he fled from Pharaoh and settled “in the land of Midian.”
Acts has God say “I have heard their groaning”; Exodus says God “heard their groaning” and remembered His covenant.
Acts repeats “Take off your sandals” and “the place where you are standing is holy ground”; Exodus gives them as God’s words.
Acts speaks of “The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob”; in Exodus, God says “I am the God of your father.”
Acts repeats “I am the God of your fathers”; Exodus has “I am the God of your father,” and Moses hides his face.
Acts repeats “I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt”; Exodus has the same words, with “affliction” for “oppression.”
Acts says “have come down to deliver them”; Exodus says “I have come down to rescue them” from the Egyptians.
Acts has “I will send you back to Egypt”; Exodus has “I am sending you to Pharaoh” to bring the Israelites out.
Acts says they will “worship Me in this place”; Exodus says that after they leave Egypt, all of them “will worship God on this mountain.”
Acts names “the God of our fathers”; in Exodus, God tells Moses to say to the Israelites, “the God of your fathers.”
Acts repeats “the God of your fathers”; Exodus has these words from God, and adds “This is My name forever.”
Acts says “You made the heaven and the earth and the sea”; Exodus says the LORD made “the heavens and the earth and the sea.”
Acts says God “made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them”; Exodus says the LORD made them in six days.
Acts says it is written, “Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people”; Exodus has “curse the ruler of your people.”
Acts repeats “Make us gods who will go before us” said to Aaron; Exodus has the people gather around Aaron and say it.
Acts repeats “Make us gods who will go before us”; in Exodus, a man says they told him this.
Acts says “He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness”; Deuteronomy says the LORD carried them “as a man carries his son.”
Acts says God defeated “seven nations in Canaan” and gave their land to His people; Deuteronomy names “seven nations larger and stronger than you.”
Acts has Moses say what Deuteronomy records: God will raise up “a prophet like me from among your brothers.”
Acts repeats Moses’ promise of “a prophet like me from among your brothers,” found in Deuteronomy.
Acts has Moses say “listen to Him in everything”; in Deuteronomy 18:16 the people say “Let us not hear the voice of the LORD.”
Acts warns that “Everyone who does not listen” will be cut off; Deuteronomy says, “I will hold accountable anyone who does not listen.”
Acts has God say “a man after My own heart”; 1 Samuel says the LORD sought “a man after His own heart.”
Acts says God promised to “place one of his descendants on his throne”; 2 Samuel says “I will raise up your descendant after you.”
Acts says David “was buried with his fathers”; 1 Kings says “David rested with his fathers” and “was buried in the City of David.”
Acts repeats the question “Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?” from Psalms.
Acts repeats “The kings of the earth take their stand”; Psalms says they gather “against the LORD and against His Anointed One.”
Acts repeats “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father,” which it says is written in the second Psalm.
Acts says God “will judge the world with justice”; Psalms says “He judges the world with justice.”
Acts has David say “He is at my right hand, I will not be shaken”; Psalms 16:8 has the same words.
Acts repeats “Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices”; the body will dwell “in hope” in Acts and “securely” in Psalms.
Acts repeats “nor will You let Your Holy One see decay,” but names “Hades” where Psalms 16:10 says “Sheol.”
Acts says the Christ “was not abandoned to Hades, nor did His body see decay”; Psalms says “You will not abandon my soul.”
Acts says “You will not let Your Holy One see decay”; Psalms 16:10 has “nor will You let Your Holy One see decay.”
Acts repeats “You will fill me with joy in Your presence”; Psalms 16:11 has the same words and adds “eternal pleasures at Your right hand.”
Acts says “God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles”; Psalms 67:2 speaks of “Your salvation among all nations.”
Acts says “May his place be deserted”; Psalms 69:25 says “May their place be deserted.”
Acts says God “had promised him on oath”; Psalms 89:3 says “I have sworn to David My servant.”
Acts says God would “place one of his descendants on his throne”; Psalms 89:4 says “I will establish your offspring forever.”
Acts has God say “I have found David son of Jesse”; Psalms 89:20 says “I have found My servant David.”
Acts repeats the words of Psalms: “May another take his position”.
Acts says David did not ascend into heaven but himself says the words in Psalms: “Sit at My right hand”.
Acts repeats the rest of the words in Psalms: “until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet”.
Acts says Jesus is the stone “you builders rejected”, using the words of Psalms about the stone that “has become the cornerstone”.
Acts says God promised on oath to place “one of his descendants on his throne”; Psalms has “One of your descendants I will place”.
Acts has believers pray to God, who made “the sea and everything in them”; Psalms calls Him “the Maker of heaven and earth”.
Acts repeats Psalms, saying the living God “made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them”.
Acts repeats Isaiah: “ever hearing but never understanding” and “ever seeing but never perceiving”.
Acts repeats Isaiah: “see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts”.
Acts says of David, “he will carry out My will in its entirety”; Isaiah says Cyrus, “My shepherd,” will do “all that I desire.”
Acts speaks of Gentiles “called by My name” who seek the Lord; Isaiah has the words “There is no other God but Me.”
Acts says these things “have been known for ages”; Isaiah asks who foretold and announced them “long ago” and “from ancient times.”
Acts repeats Isaiah’s words about a “light” to bring salvation “to the ends of the earth,” naming the Gentiles where Isaiah has the nations.
Acts repeats Isaiah’s words about one led “to the slaughter” who “did not open His mouth,” like a silent lamb or sheep.
Acts repeats Isaiah’s question about who “can recount His descendants,” and says His life was removed from the earth.
Acts has “I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David”; Isaiah has an everlasting covenant, “My loving devotion promised to David.”
Acts repeats Isaiah’s words “Heaven is My throne” and “What kind of house will you build for Me?”
Acts repeats Isaiah’s question “Has not My hand made all these things?”
Acts repeats Joel’s words “I will pour out My Spirit on all people,” with sons and daughters prophesying.
Acts repeats Joel’s words “Even on My menservants and maidservants” and “I will pour out My Spirit in those days.”
Acts repeats Joel’s words “I will show wonders in the heavens,” with “billows of smoke” where Joel says “columns of smoke.”
Acts repeats Joel’s words “The sun will be turned to darkness” and the moon to blood before the Day of the Lord.
Acts says “everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved”; Joel says “The sun will be turned to darkness.”
Acts repeats Amos’s question “Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness.”
Acts repeats Amos’s words “You have taken along” and “the idols you made,” but names Molech and Rephan where Amos names Sakkuth and Kaiwan.
Acts repeats Amos’s words “Therefore I will send you into exile beyond,” ending with Babylon where Amos says Damascus.
Acts repeats Amos’s words about “the fallen tent of David,” its ruins, and a promise to rebuild and restore it.
Acts has “the remnant of men” and “called by My name”; Amos has “the remnant of Edom” and nations “that bear My name.”
Acts says these things “have been known for ages”; Amos says the LORD is the one “who will do this.”
Acts repeats Habakkuk’s words “a work in your days that you would never believe.”
Acts repeats Psalms: “You will not let Your Holy One see decay”; Psalms also has “You will not abandon my soul to Sheol”.
Acts has Moses say “a prophet like me from among your brothers”; Deuteronomy says “a prophet like you from among their brothers.”
Acts repeats “a prophet like me from among your brothers”; Deuteronomy says “a prophet like you from among their brothers.”
Acts repeats the man’s question “Who made you ruler and judge over us?”; Exodus has the same words, and Moses is afraid.
Acts has “a light for the Gentiles”; Isaiah has the LORD say “a light to the nations.”
